Insider selling is routine 10b5-1 plan activity only. The digest's net_debt_to_ebitda of -3.37x (net cash) is from the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 and PRE-DATES the Chart Industries close on 2026-07-16 -- post-close leverage is materially higher than this trailing figure, though $3.1B TTM free cash flow supports rapid deleveraging. original_plan.thesis: DexCom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.308B (+13% YoY reported, +12% organic, per the 2026-07-30 earnings release), beat EPS estimates by 15.1% (fourth straight beat), and raised full-year revenue guidance to $5.18-5.25B while lifting non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 23.5-24% -- GAAP operating margin already expanded 590bps YoY to 24.3% this quarter. Note: the bundle's digest field states 26.3% YoY revenue growth for DXCM, which conflicts with the source earnings release's own stated 13%/12% organic figure -- I am citing the sourced, lower number as the reliable one and flagging the discrepancy rather than using the more flattering figure. The balance sheet is net cash (-0.81x net debt/EBITDA, $1.95B cash, minimal debt), TTM free cash flow more than doubled to $1.405B, and the company is returning capital (3.88% TTM buyback yield, diluted shares down 4.4% YoY). Ownership_flow shows institutional accumulation aligned with the rising price, and sell-side has been raising targets all week (BTIG to $90, Stifel to $95, Truist to $93, WebSearch-verified, not bundle-sourced) following the print. The stock pulled back 4.92% in its most recent session after tagging a 52-week high three sessions earlier -- I could not confirm a specific negative catalyst for that single-session drop through today's degraded news feed, so I am treating it as digestion after a strong run (RSI 61.5, not overbought; still above both the 50- and 200-day averages) rather than a broken thesis, and sizing/stopping so that I am proven wrong cheaply if it is more than that.

performance_breakdown.note: Your own results by category - weight your confidence using this evidence. Rates are WITHHELD (null) below the sample floor - counts are facts, a win rate off two trades is not.

calibration.note: Realized win rate vs the confidence you STATED at entry, by bucket. A large negative calibration_gap_pct means your confidence is inflated; cap stated confidence until the gap closes (per the Learning Protocol).

target_calibration.note: Grades the claim behind min_risk_reward_ratio. Targets stay NON-BINDING for exits (letting winners run is correct); this measures whether the claimed RR was ever real. rr_inflation is WITHHELD until the sample binds.
